Each step is one lane, reviewed, promoted by the operator because it changes the tool that promotes.

Its 14 unique commits were the Sep 30 items-pane line (superseded by items-observe on main), a delegation-queue WIP with a failing test, and docs/reports EVALUATION- and HANDOFF-operator-alignment-2026-09-30.md, whose conclusions the 2026-10-01 decision model replaced. ENG-66's worker may mine the tag for items-pane ideas.
decisions.summary: block-review archived: superseded or unfinished, recoverable from its tag.

decisions.text: Keep .org/, ORG_DIR, ORG_ACTOR, the org project-config key, event fields and existing paths unchanged.
decisions.why: They are durable compatibility and integration surfaces. Renaming them would split discovery and configuration into two sources without improving what an adopter sees.

decisions.text: Define permanent alias to mean exact behavior, with no warning, deprecation message or org-specific output.
decisions.why: Both entry points execute bin/org.mjs, and the parity test checks identical status, signal, stdout and stderr for every dispatched command.

decisions.text: Keep bin/org.mjs as the implementation and add bin/record.mjs as the public entry point.
decisions.why: Existing absolute paths and the bch-cloak symlink remain valid, while new users get the chosen name. Moving the implementation would add churn and compatibility machinery with no visible benefit.

decisions.text: Add record to future release launchers and make newly created launchers removable by release restore.
decisions.why: npm packaging alone would not install the command in the release path this project actually uses; restore must still return the machine to its exact pre-activation launcher set.

decisions.text: Remove the separate bin/record.mjs wrapper and install both record and org as aliases of bin/org.mjs.
decisions.why: The wrapper's relative import only worked in its source tree, so copying it onto PATH created a broken command. Direct aliases make behavior structural and retain the unchanged internal implementation path.

decisions.text: Extend an existing release before directory one launcher at a time.
decisions.why: Older snapshots legitimately lack entries for launcher names introduced by later releases; saving each previously unseen launcher's state preserves exact restore without overwriting prior evidence.

decisions.text: Keep canary and release command installation separate.
decisions.why: herdr/canary-env.sh scopes the canary bin to this repository, while ~/.local/bin is the release launcher directory shared by other projects.

decisions.text: Treat only an activation-shaped symlink into the release home’s current tree as removable when a launcher was originally absent.
decisions.why: A regular file or user link installed later is new operator state and restore must not destroy it.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main 398b633 after three review rounds (r3 PASS; its three Minor wording leftovers fixed by the supervisor in 94f1a11, gate green). Canary now has record -> main bin/org.mjs beside org and lane in ~/.local/share/herdr-monitor/canary/bin; record and org give identical show --json. ~/.local/bin and the active release untouched: bch-cloak gets record only when a release is activated. Lane closed.
decisions.summary: record name promoted to main and live on the canary; release untouched.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main 529068d after four rounds (reviews r1-r3 NEEDS-WORK, each narrower; r4's diff checked by the supervisor directly, gate green, to save a fourth Opus review). First real use: armed on R-33 at 15:28 with 'node watch/watch.mjs R-33 --org <record> --to supervisor-herdr --spawn' from the main checkout; a shell wait stays as backstop for this one run. Lane closed. Retiring settle-watch, Brain watch and bch-cloak's notify-watch remains ENG-64.
decisions.summary: watch promoted; first real use on R-33.

decisions.text: Keep projects as scope and goals/work blocks as optional context; make typed items and their lifecycle the work shown inside that frame.
decisions.why: A project answers where work belongs, while the record's items answer what agents created and what needs attention. Replacing one with the other would discard useful context; making a human-maintained goal list authoritative would violate the operating model.

decisions.text: Carry lifecycle activity and item provenance into the modern console, but not transcript indexing, aliases, state filters or supervisor-message actions.
decisions.why: The modern console already shows current state, sessions and decisions from durable sources. The omitted features made chat text a second index of work or routed action indirectly through the supervisor, duplicating the record and Brain paths.

decisions.text: Reduce contrib to settle-watch and give every other file a named home or retirement.
decisions.why: contrib had become a mixture of live compatibility code, supervisor housekeeping, stale prototypes and historical evidence.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: first real use passed. R-33's worker stopped ~15:36; the watcher (armed 15:28) delivered '[org-report] run=R-33 … check=pass' to supervisor-herdr and closed its own tab. The shell backstop woke at the same time; the supervisor drops the backstop from here on and arms watch/watch.mjs --spawn per run.
decisions.summary: watch proven on a real run; shell backstop retired.

decisions.text: Identify Activity controls as activity:<event sequence>, while resolving Enter and clicks back to the durable item.
decisions.why: The sequence distinguishes every chronological moment without changing the item page that a moment opens. Detail and summary lines remain mouse targets but are not additional keyboard stops.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main 6b353db after two review rounds (r2 PASS; its one Minor, dropped questions shown as answered, fixed by the supervisor with a test, gate green). Standalone items pane retired; Activity view and item provenance live in the modern console; contrib/ reduced to settle-watch. Lane closed.
decisions.summary: one console on main.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr, 2026-10-01: Phase 3 opens. Order stays routes, watch, housekeeping, dispatch, settle, promote, supervisor, but watch is already built here (ENG-67), so its remaining step is the bch-cloak switch, which needs a release. First moves: (1) routes module: one route table and selection policy read by lane dispatch, replacing the values copied outside routing.json that the inventory names; (2) ENG-64: retire settle-watch and Brain watch here in favour of watch/, and plan bch-cloak's notify-watch switch for a quiet point. Each switch in bch-cloak waits on a release the operator activates.
decisions.summary: Phase 3 starts with routes and retiring this repo's extra watchers.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr, 2026-10-01: release candidate v0.1.3 tagged (annotated, local, not pushed) at 6b353db and built into releases/v0.1.3; NOT activated, so bch-cloak still runs v0.1.2. Evidence it ran here: the record name (ENG-65, R-27/30/32), the watch module delivering real reports for R-33 and R-35 (ENG-67), and the console fold (ENG-66) were all used on the canary by the supervisor today. Activation is the operator's call: herdr/release.sh activate v0.1.3 (rollback: release.sh rollback).
decisions.summary: v0.1.3 built, not activated; activation waits on the operator.

decisions.text: Retire settle-watch as a watcher and keep its distinct model-session launch behavior under supervisor.
decisions.why: Waiting for a worker and telling the supervisor is watch's job; account selection, session brakes, routing, prompts and ledgers are launch policy and remain useful without observing worker lifecycle.

decisions.text: Make final report delivery and settle-session launch two explicit steps.
decisions.why: watch/watch.mjs delivers the validated report to supervisor-herdr, whose protocol then invokes supervisor/settle.sh once; this preserves fresh-context settlement without a second watcher.

decisions.text: Keep Brain watch unchanged.
decisions.why: Its consumer is the operator and console, its input is every stopped Herdr session's screen, and its durable output is the private Brain queue; watch/watch.mjs instead follows one recorded run and delivers a validated report to a supervisor.

decisions.text: Gate every bch-cloak change on release activation and a quiet point.
decisions.why: Its dispatch currently calls notify-watch.sh directly, its copied supervisor launch wrapper names the retired canonical path, and changing either while runs are active could leave a run with zero or two watchers.

decisions.text: Operator, 2026-10-01: engineering routes move to gpt-6.1-sol; gpt-5.6-sol archived. supervisor-herdr changed /Users/rewt/development/rewt/.lane.json (dispatch default, engineer, engineer-max, engineer-xhigh; terra and luna unchanged), kept the old file as .lane.json.bak-20261001-sol-5.6, and updated lanes/docs/REFERENCE.md. Runs from R-38 on use 6.1; R-36 (routes) started on 5.6 and finishes on it.
decisions.summary: Engineering routes on gpt-6.1-sol; 5.6 archived as a backup file.

decisions.text: Restore the original settle-watch implementation instead of building a forwarding shim.
decisions.why: Exact restoration proves the hard-coded external caller retains its current CLI, waiting behavior, session handoff, brakes and route handling without relying on assumptions about which arguments bch-cloak uses.

decisions.text: Keep the compatibility watcher out of Herdr Monitor's own supervisor flow.
decisions.why: supervisor/arm-watch.sh still calls watch/watch.mjs and supervisor/settle.sh still calls open-session.mjs, preserving the one-watcher design inside this repository while the external caller transitions.

decisions.text: Remove the compatibility file only after bch-cloak's release-gated canary succeeds.
decisions.why: Removing it earlier makes a main fast-forward alter bch-cloak outside release activation; removing it last makes both the cutover and rollback explicit.

decisions.text: Keep routing configuration inside the existing layered lane configuration, with its validation and resolution in a dedicated dependency-free lanes/routes.mjs module.
decisions.why: Lane and record can share one implementation without introducing a second project configuration file or making the record understand any model or provider.

decisions.text: A named route owns harness, model, and effort; manual harness/model/effort flags cannot override it.
decisions.why: Allowing per-launch overrides would recreate the drift this item removes. Unrouted legacy record and lane calls remain supported.

decisions.text: Treat selection-policy task classes and pools as opaque names and validate only their references to routes.
decisions.why: The mapping mechanism is reusable, while bch-cloak's provider pools and policy prose are its own operational choices.

decisions.text: Infer effort from legacy native arguments only when no explicit effort field exists, and make explicit route metadata win at launch.
decisions.why: Herdr-brain's shared config keeps working without editing it, while the richer kit schema remains authoritative and sessions agree with run metadata.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: settlement found the lane changed contrib/settle-watch.mjs to refuse --model/--effort, which bch-cloak's launch-supervisor.mjs passes when it calls that file by absolute path in this checkout; promoting would have broken bch-cloak when main moved. The supervisor reverted that file and its test on the lane (33a6499) and noted it in the report; settle-watch moves onto lanes/routes.mjs with ENG-64's release-gated switch. Second time today (R-37 too): briefs for this repo must say that bch-cloak calls contrib/settle-watch.mjs by path.
decisions.summary: settle-watch left as bch-cloak calls it; routes otherwise unchanged.

decisions.text: Refuse rather than wait when another settle or executive session is working.
decisions.why: open-session runs in the long-running supervisor's foreground; an unbounded wait would make the supervisor unavailable. The protocol now keeps the original report notice, blocks on the named session reaching a terminal state, and retries the exact settle command.

decisions.text: Add idle grace to the generic watcher but leave cleanup and supervisor naming in bch-cloak policy.
decisions.why: Delaying only a no-report notice is reusable watcher behavior and allows the existing 900-second setting; closing tabs and maintaining a project-specific supervisor identity belong to housekeeping and session bootstrap.

decisions.text: Treat per-run watcher logs as bch-cloak's post-cutover recovery ledger.
decisions.why: watch logs every notice before attempting delivery, so tidy-tabs can surface swallowed prompts without adding a second shared log or project-specific writes to the generic watcher.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main 88ee2f6 after review r2 PASS. settle-watch's waiting moved to watch/; its session launch is supervisor/open-session.mjs behind settle.sh and continue.sh; contrib/settle-watch.mjs unchanged for bch-cloak. Brain watch kept (operator queue, different job). The supervisor reworded KICKOFF so settling in place or via settle.sh stays the supervisor's choice. The r2 Minors only matter when idle grace is on (bch-cloak's switch), so they became a follow-up item that gates that switch. The bch-cloak cutover plan is in docs/reports/ENG-64-one-watcher-20261001.md.
decisions.summary: one watcher on main; bch-cloak switch planned, gated on a release.

decisions.text: Separate declared metadata resolution from native launch resolution in the same dependency-free module.
decisions.why: The record uses resolveRoute without harness-specific branches; only lane's resolveLaunchRoute infers legacy effort and checks native argument collisions.

decisions.text: Supply a verified shared-config patch rather than editing the shared configuration.
decisions.why: The ask explicitly prohibits editing /Users/rewt/development/rewt/.lane.json. ENG-69 already owns that migration, so no duplicate proposal is needed.

decisions.text: Keep the settle watcher and its tests unchanged.
decisions.why: AGENTS.md protects its existing bch-cloak callers until ENG-64's release-gated switch.

decisions.text: Compare Codex config defaults by normalized key rather than by the repeatable option name.
decisions.why: Defaults for unrelated keys must reach the launch while an explicitly supplied or emitted value suppresses a fallback for that same key.

decisions.text: Reject all caller-supplied profiles and profiles.* overrides on named routes.
decisions.why: Rejecting the profile configuration namespace also covers table assignments and prevents profile-scoped settings from bypassing route authority. Trusted project configuration remains supported.

decisions.text: Use commit subject lines for every commit citation in all three ENG-68 reports.
decisions.why: The supervisor may rebase the lane after reporting; commit hashes then change even when their patches do not.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main 9436e3d after rounds 1-2 reviewed (NEEDS-WORK) and round 3's diff checked by the supervisor (all-Minor findings; gate green). lanes/routes.mjs resolves routes for lane dispatch and record start --route; the record copies only declared kind/model/effort; native-argument handling stays in lane. settle-watch untouched for bch-cloak. Lane closed.
decisions.summary: routes module on main.

decisions.text: Keep dispatch as a foreground module at dispatch/dispatch.mjs, composing the record, lane and watch CLIs with argument arrays.
decisions.why: The record remains deterministic, library-free and foreground. Lane retains ownership and lifecycle checks; only the existing watcher runs in the background.

decisions.text: Arm and acknowledge the watcher before sending the generated work prompt.
decisions.why: Starting a worker without a prompt allows its identity to be recorded first and makes watch failure retryable without starting unwatched work.

decisions.text: Store dispatch progress in its own atomic request journal and describe milestones and errors through record notes.
decisions.why: Recovery needs durable knowledge of ambiguous side effects, while item and run status must remain derived from the record's events. No stored core status or new event type is introduced.

decisions.text: Freeze routing per request and require explicit stopped-worker reuse from an earlier run.
decisions.why: Record and launch use one route snapshot. Fix rounds cannot silently reuse a worker on a different model or infer permission from session display metadata.

decisions.text: Require caller inspection and explicit adoption, fresh launch, acceptance or resend when an external side effect has an uncertain outcome.
decisions.why: Neither a CLI failure nor an interrupted response proves that its side effect did not happen. Blind retries could create duplicate workers or deliver the same work twice.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main 7575ca8 after review r1 PASS. dispatch/dispatch.mjs replaces the supervisor's five hand steps; four Minor recovery edges (stranded retry at 'starting', run id accepted as item, retry lock race, reuse while the prior run is open) became ENG-72, which is dispatched with the module itself as its first live use. Lane closed.
decisions.summary: dispatch module on main; first live use is its own hardening.

decisions.text: Reconcile starting requests through record show, adopting exactly one matching run and restarting only a known record refusal with no match.
decisions.why: This recovers deterministic refusals and lost replies without creating duplicate runs. Unknown outcomes with no match and multiple matches still require explicit inspection and recovery.

decisions.text: Publish unique PID contenders before inspecting or replacing the original PID lock, and read retry progress only after acquisition.
decisions.why: Later contenders see the live claimant and refuse. Stale contender names are never reused, so crash cleanup cannot unlink a new claimant. A crash during either acquisition phase remains recoverable; simultaneous contenders may conservatively both refuse.

decisions.text: Require the previous reuse run to be reported or abandoned at preflight and again before binding the worker.
decisions.why: Invalid reuse creates no lane or run, and retries still enforce the same durable prerequisite alongside the existing routing and occupant checks.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main after the supervisor checked the diff (four Minor findings from a PASS review, each with a regression test; gate green). R-43 was the dispatch module's first live use: record, journal, watcher and prompt agreed, confirmed from both sides. Lane closed.
decisions.summary: dispatch hardening on main; dispatch module proven live.

decisions.text: Operator, 2026-10-01: before anything goes to bch-cloak, design local test cases that show things work as expected. supervisor-herdr: made it a release gate (ENG-74): no bch-cloak switch until its cases pass against the candidate release. Design choice: real Herdr, git, record and release code with scripted stand-in workers (no model calls), so the whole cycle runs end to end repeatably; an optional live smoke on a cheap route stays manual.
decisions.summary: Local end-to-end release acceptance (ENG-74) gates every bch-cloak switch.

decisions.text: Operator, 2026-10-01, on the frame: this is designed for anyone to use with any project, not for bch-cloak. A project needs no specific user configuration: agents discover it when they enter a project to work, and the project's record populates from the work they do; everything agentic. supervisor-herdr: re-centred ENG-74 (release acceptance) on a brand-new project with nothing set up, bch-cloak as one existing project among others; steered R-46 mid-run. Today's Phase 3 briefs leaned on bch-cloak as the reference; later briefs start from the unconfigured project, and ARCH-10 (adoption) is where hand configuration that remains gets removed.
decisions.summary: Any project, no setup, agent-discovered: the frame for every module and test.

decisions.text: Require observed working before idle grace and include blocked in its blocking wait.
decisions.why: This matches the documented lifecycle contract and prevents a fifteen-minute delay in reporting a newly blocked worker during bch-cloak's planned grace.

decisions.text: Keep bch-cloak changes as a release-gated plan, including continuation and settle retries.
decisions.why: This run fixes prerequisites in this lane; the operator still controls release activation and the quiet-point switch.

decisions.text: Leave KICKOFF.md unchanged.
decisions.why: Its existing Reports reach you paragraph already tells the supervisor to keep a refused settle notice and retry after the busy session stops, with a link to SETTLE.md.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main; diff checked directly (idle grace now gated on observedWorking and wakes on blocked, with fixture tests; cutover plan carries continue.sh's wait-to-refusal change, the retry rule and a check). bch-cloak's watcher switch is now gated only on ENG-74's acceptance and a release the operator activates.
decisions.summary: watch parity on main; watcher switch now waits on ENG-74 and a release.

decisions.text: Operator, 2026-10-01: a main use case is that agents discover the lane policy, run several sessions side by side without collision, follow the promotion process, and ask the operator how to configure model routing with today's routes as the suggested default. supervisor-herdr: added as primary cases (brief ae57e6f); these need real agents on the cheapest workable route, so they are the one place the acceptance run spends tokens; steered R-46.
decisions.summary: Discovery, side-by-side lanes, promotion and a routing question are primary acceptance cases.

decisions.text: Default housekeeping on and discover the project, record and base branch; configuration is an optional override.
decisions.why: The operator's steering superseded the brief's switch-on premise. Git worktree discovery and the existing record discovery provide the necessary machine-specific values without requiring a project setup file.

decisions.text: Use a project-scoped deterministic timer started idempotently by an entering agent or supervisor.
decisions.why: A 60-second recovery tick and 600-second cleanup pass cover record ingestion and later Git promotion, neither of which is fully represented by Herdr events or watch's final notice. No launchd installation or resident reasoning session is required.

decisions.text: Reuse the tidy-tabs planner with explicit record and Git authorization for every live worker in a tab.
decisions.why: Tab topology, running-process protection, watcher cleanup and self-tab protection already exist there. Strict mode prevents its legacy report-only or review/session-file rules from authorizing housekeeping deletion.

decisions.text: Recover only the evidenced accidental mouse-wheel interruption, with a durable attempt written before input.
decisions.why: A bare idle worker can be finished, waiting or interrupted by a human. The current banner plus an exclusively wheel-junk composer narrows automatic recovery to the incident demonstrated by the existing kit, and uncertain input must not be replayed after restart.

decisions.text: Store module bookkeeping beside the discovered record, separated by canonical repository identity.
decisions.why: Default-on operation must not create untracked files that make a project with no ignore configuration dirty. Housekeeping never writes events.jsonl or stored work status.

decisions.text: Refuse live startup from linked worktree code instead of silently re-executing another checkout's script.
decisions.why: A worker's checkout must not install unreviewed code as the project schedule. Refusal makes the runtime choice explicit while allowing the supervisor to use canonical code or an installed plugin/release without project configuration.

decisions.text: Apply the provenance guard to both --start and --loop, including a record CLI override, and require a canonical target checkout.
decisions.why: Guarding only the detached wrapper leaves a foreground-loop bypass or a removable record executable. Lane workers retain isolated --once --dry-run previews.

decisions.text: Include resolved script and record_cli paths in lock ownership and refuse mismatched, missing or legacy runtime identities.
decisions.why: Later callers must not mistake a surviving PID running removed lane code for a healthy matching schedule. Refusal preserves the old lock and never kills an existing process; the supervisor can inspect and stop it before restarting.

decisions.text: Recognize a current interruption by scanning backward through trailing blank and feedback-hint rows, then checking one banner row.
decisions.why: This preserves the current-banner distinction while making processing linear in the visible screen size and avoiding synchronous lock-holding hangs.

decisions.text: Gate every non-dry-run CLI mode with the existing stable-runtime and canonical-target checks.
decisions.why: The safety boundary follows whether a command can act on live panes, including a one-pass invocation. Dry-run previews retain unrestricted linked-worktree source and target discovery.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main a235a15 after review r2 PASS and r3's one-line guard checked directly. Default-on, discovered, no config. A dry-run pass from the canonical checkout would close nothing (10 tabs kept, each with a reason). Started live from the canonical checkout at 19:02 (pid 8021, state under .org/housekeeping/); stop with SIGTERM or enabled=false in .housekeeping.json. Lane closed.
decisions.summary: housekeeping on main and running here.

decisions.text: Make pristine-project discovery the primary gate and keep configured mechanics and existing-project compatibility separate cases.
decisions.why: Passing an explicitly configured fixture cannot prove a project needs no user setup. Real agents must discover policy and populate the record from their work.

decisions.text: Use native ephemeral Codex sessions on gpt-5.6-luna low only for discovery, with no automatic model escalation.
decisions.why: This was the cheapest declared workable route and completed the overlapping coding tasks. It can establish absence of discoverable policy without paying for the engineer route. All mechanics stay scripted and outside npm test.

decisions.text: Keep pending cases and harness failures visible and make any failure or pending case exit 1.
decisions.why: The acceptance kit is delivered but incomplete. The operator must not infer that either candidate is safe to switch from passing mechanics or byte restoration.

decisions.text: Restrict control to opaque creation receipts and scratch paths, retaining native workspace-write protection.
decisions.why: Unknown targets, symlink escapes, services and focus changes are denied. Shell readiness must be fixed within scratch rather than typing into an uncertain pane or bypassing sandbox protection.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: R-46 delivered the gate (acceptance/run.mjs): main 13 pass / 7 fail / 2 pending, v0.1.3 7/4/11, both NOT READY. Configured cycle, failure paths, fix rounds, watch cutover and release mechanics pass; the core failure is discovery (fresh projects: no policy found, agents work in the shared checkout, no record, no routing question). Real-agent cases on gpt-5.6-luna low cost ~240k input tokens per full run, mostly cached. Next: ENG-77 discovery dispatched first (R-49, engineer-xhigh), judged by cases 02-04, 20, 21; the harness itself is in review (its ~120 committed evidence files are a question for review).
decisions.summary: Acceptance gate built; discovery is the blocker, ENG-77 started.

decisions.text: Deliver policy through machine launch adapters instead of copying instruction files into every project.
decisions.why: The installed adapter reaches a pristine unrelated project before the model acts, can create the lane before sandbox startup, and distinguishes an explicitly selected supervisor from default workers. Codex and Claude prompt transport stay outside the neutral runtime and record core.

decisions.text: Bootstrap the record on trusted entry or first record use, with canonical Git identity and race-safe initialization.
decisions.why: Linked worktrees share the canonical record, concurrent initialization cannot truncate events, and the adapter ignores inherited record and explicit route-file overrides from unrelated sessions. Legacy ancestor records still work. Passive console discovery remains unchanged.

decisions.text: Ship today's portable routes as suggestions and require a real operator answer before persisting them.
decisions.why: The other question category is used with the generic record ask --wait option, so even an auto-answer override cannot silently choose model preferences. Yes applies the proposed preset; no leaves it unapplied; valid route JSON supports a custom answer. Personal paths, profiles and accounts are excluded.

decisions.text: Keep a foreground session parent with fixed Git capabilities and sandbox all project preparation and validation.
decisions.why: Requests cannot supply arbitrary commands, Git argv, repositories or cwd. Identity and branch receipts are checked on every operation. Git hooks, signing and fsmonitor are disabled; external filters and drivers are refused before checkout. Existing clean/rebase/green/fast-forward promotion checks remain intact, with no push or automatic deletion.

decisions.text: Preserve failed probes and judge this lane through an independent installed-product test while R-50 corrects the release harness.
decisions.why: The supervisor identified source-adjacency contamination in the unpromoted acceptance lane. This run did not edit or claim that harness green. Product installation and projects use separate scratch roots, and the final transcript command audit found zero references to either herdr-brain source checkout.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: R-49's design: discovery through machine-installed entry adapters on Herdr's shell PATH (wrapping codex/claude launch), not files in each project; record auto-created on first use in a Git project; routes shipped as a suggested preset applied only after an operator answer (record ask --wait, category other); workers in their own lanes with a bounded Git-capable parent for promotion; supervisor role only from the canonical checkout. Four real Luna sessions discovered it in unrelated scratch projects. In review; to weigh: ~90 committed probe evidence files, and record auto-initializing on read commands. Installing the adapters on this machine is a machine-level change for the operator to approve after review.
decisions.summary: Discovery via installed entry adapters; in review; machine install awaits the operator.

decisions.text: Fail closed before any copied code executes, then enforce an independent kernel boundary.
decisions.why: Text relocation alone cannot constrain a dynamically computed record or code path. Require a matched launcher replacement, audit every transitive copied file before each invocation, pin a scratch ORG_DIR and deny external writes and host project contents.

decisions.text: Separate fresh project parents from all harness and candidate artifacts, and require actual product policy attribution.
decisions.why: First-round find .. exposed candidate AGENTS.md and module READMEs. A reported lane string or no-policy assertion is insufficient; successful tool output or a captured installed-adapter delivery must substantiate the source.

decisions.text: Use the candidate's machine installer and native entry shim when shipped, with a transparent transport receipt.
decisions.why: Bypassing the installed entry adapter would falsely reject project-entry delivery. The transport contributes no policy; it records supplied developer instructions, refuses foreign roots and reapplies the native permission boundary to validation.

decisions.text: Keep the unresolved metadata finding bounded and revise the historical report and proposal.
decisions.why: Immediate lookup was an inadequate test. The final poll found no worktree metadata in 85 main samples and 78 older-release samples over a 15-second timeout, so wrappers were not run. Later readiness remains possible.

decisions.text: Restrict implicit PATH entry to fresh interactive launches and retain explicit monitor entry for deliberate batch use.
decisions.why: Existing launchers already own their role, checkout, run and report topology. Batch discovery probes now opt in through monitor-codex instead of intercepting every codex exec invocation.

decisions.text: Harden shared file operations and resolve canonical validation fields independently.
decisions.why: Routes, replies, audit records, gate files and report reads must not follow agent-created redirects. Canonical validate and prepare remain authoritative whenever each field is present; lane values are fallback only.

decisions.text: Preserve summaries in Git and retain raw historical and current verification evidence in scratch.
decisions.why: Transcripts, tested-product snapshots and test logs are review evidence rather than product source. Existing follow-on items already cover release installation, native Herdr interception and real Claude coverage.

decisions.text: Exercise the actual machine-installed headless entry and its bounded Git parent.
decisions.why: The candidate installer supplies monitor-codex; the gate invokes its documented -- exec interface. Normal automatic interactive PATH entry deliberately passes headless codex exec through. Project workflow configuration is never supplied by the fixture.

decisions.text: Separate harness refusal from candidate failure on the one-screen.
decisions.why: Capability, ownership, native transport and interrupted-session limits become PENDING with [HARNESS] and a reason. Missing shipped discovery remains a product FAIL after native capability checks pass.

decisions.text: Treat the captured adapter delivery as the authoritative policy source.
decisions.why: A real host transport records the candidate's supplied developer instructions and installed source. Model paraphrases cannot manufacture or invalidate that receipt; the real case additionally requires separate lanes, recorded work and successful integration.

decisions.text: Narrow the existing workspace identity handoff instead of declaring a startup race fixed.

decisions.text: Normalize absent record paths in the existing shared CLI environment helper.
decisions.why: Both housekeeping adapters use it; clearing the inherited override lets the validating CLI discover the selected project's record or return its no-record defaults.

decisions.text: Display command failures and planned reasons separately in both housekeeping readers.
decisions.why: The planned eligibility reason cannot explain a failed close; independent rendering preserves the failure and its context.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main after review r1 (review-codex) and r2's diff checked directly (absent record clears ORG_DIR instead of passing 'null'; close failures show the error, then the reason), on retry after a load flake (load average 20). The console shows housekeeping activity and lets the operator pause it or change overrides through the CLI.
decisions.summary: console-housekeeping promoted to main.

decisions.text: Normalize omitted arguments only for the ready tool before SDK input validation.
decisions.why: A name-only ready call has no required inputs, while role filtering, strict argument checks and required-input tools retain their existing schemas and behavior.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main after review r1 (review-codex) and r2's diff checked directly (name-only record_ready calls normalized before SDK validation). A foreground stdio MCP server in mcp/ exposes the record CLI (ready, show, add, ask, answer, start, check, ingest; snapshot as a resource) through argument arrays; its dependencies (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod) are pinned and isolated from the dependency-free core. Follow-up: release builds should install mcp/ dependencies like console/, and the omitted-arguments normalization could cover every tool.
decisions.summary: mcp-server promoted to main.

decisions.text: Require the requested run's matching recorded report receipt before advancing settlement, resuming pending work or returning saved readiness.
decisions.why: CLI exit status alone cannot establish ingestion. The record's immutable receipt distinguishes skipped intake, missing intake and a different report before settlement changes the item or launches review.

decisions.text: Reconcile a unique recorded correction linked to the matched dispatch request before checking supersession and concurrent work.
decisions.why: A committed start with a lost response leaves the journal's run unset. Exempting only its unique recorded correction lets dispatch perform its existing locked adoption while retaining closure, blocker and newer-run checks.

decisions.text: Set an explicit actor in every settlement fixture and reproduce both findings before applying the fixes.
decisions.why: The tests must exercise their own actor context. Observed promotable and terminal-escalation failures establish that the new behavior regressions detect both defects using actual record and coordination code.

decisions.text: Reject parent traversal and other unresolved or mixed foreign paths before classifying environment I/O as scratch-owned, using native realpath for containment.
decisions.why: The operator explicitly requires fail-closed classification whenever ownership is uncertain; lexical normalization must not hide a symlink escape.

decisions.text: Register each temp root immediately after creation and pass the same registry through command failures, case bodies and cutover subchecks.
decisions.why: Harness setup may throw before candidate execution in a separate owned root; a live registry preserves that ownership evidence through classification.

decisions.text: Run both requested comparisons with skip-live and retain their two pending discovery checks.
decisions.why: This is the requested fix-round scope; the supervisor already completed the full main comparison.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: fixed the discovery lifecycle flake directly ('Unexpected end of JSON input'): the test fixture wrote its receipt non-atomically and the parent parsed it on existence; now written to a temp file and renamed. It was blocking promotion gates under load. The ENG-88 worker (R-85) is told so it does not duplicate the change.
decisions.summary: lifecycle-flake promoted to main.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main after review r1 (review-codex) and r2's diff checked directly (fails closed: no '..', realpath before containment, dangling symlinks stop, every path must be in a registered scratch root), after the lifecycle flake fix. The harness runs against read-only release directories; releases/v0.1.4 24/0/0 and main 24/0/0 with real discovery (supervisor's run).
decisions.summary: release-snapshot promoted to main.

decisions.text: Reject redirected workspace, temporary, queue and live-runtime paths at the common sandbox boundary before constructing any provider exception.
decisions.why: An existing target or successful realpath is insufficient authority for a writable grant; inspect every component and retain protected-state exclusions.

decisions.text: Preserve inactive filters and use a trusted binary byte copy for an active driver's missing classic direction while requiring configured commands to succeed.
decisions.why: Git permits single-direction filters and empty commands; an empty shell loses bytes and a missing required direction aborts valid operations.

decisions.text: Classify both unexecuted live Claude cases as PENDING and leave native sessions untouched.
decisions.why: The existing operator prerequisite HUM-19 remains unanswered; absent live proof establishes neither acceptance nor a code failure.

decisions.text: Quiesce producers from a separate guardian before reading the final ledger, and start an external replacement reaper if that guardian disappears.
decisions.why: A blocked test file cannot clean itself, and outer or guardian SIGKILL must still reap a detached fixture frozen before its first registration append.

decisions.text: Refuse and report signals when a current process identity cannot be positively confirmed; retain the cleanup ledger when cleanup is unconfirmed.
decisions.why: The operator explicitly prohibited signalling recycled or unconfirmed PIDs and process groups because other sessions are live on this machine.

decisions.text: Use deterministic lookup and signal injection for failure and reuse cases, alongside real nested-process cancellation regressions and scoped read-only survivor audits.
decisions.why: Failed lookups and unrelated replacements must produce zero signal calls without risking any operator process; real subprocess tests separately prove escaped-worker cleanup.

decisions.text: Preserve main's atomic discovery receipt writer during rebase and apply the common execution bounds to main's newly added tests.
decisions.why: The supervisor confirmed the receipt fix was already on main; integration still needs every new active suite and fixture to follow the bounded execution contract.

decisions.text: Implement a content-addressed dependency-free entry runtime for plugin builds and retain existing immutable version directories as activation targets.
decisions.why: Herdr relocates its build checkout, while immutable version directories are stable and existing sessions need their original code to remain available.

decisions.text: Implement wrapper generation in scratch and apply validated machine changes through a durable recovery journal.
decisions.why: This supports the actual older installer contract and restores completed or staged writes after failure without overwriting user edits.

decisions.text: Resolve the explicit supervisor's invocation directory from Herdr context and verify canonical identity through Git.
decisions.why: The plugin pane's default working directory belongs to the plugin rather than the selected project; workspace labels and agent session metadata grant no authority.

decisions.text: Review r3 NEEDS-WORK (.lane/reviews/test-hangs/b4ffdfd-r3.md): two new Majors inside the process-guardian machinery. supervisor-herdr: four rounds of growing reaper complexity, each finding new edges; per the North Star (sophistication is usually evidence of a wrong turn), round 4 (R-94) steps back to the simplest design: per-fixture process groups with hard timeouts, no detached grandchildren in fixtures, and an end-of-suite audit that fails and names survivors instead of hunting them.
decisions.summary: ENG-88 round 4: simplify rather than add machinery.

decisions.text: Capture effective routing at settlement intake and pass it to lane review through --route-config.
decisions.why: Discovery and review otherwise disagree when a config contains only settle preferences. A routing-only snapshot shares defaults and selected model settings while preserving the original lifecycle sources.

decisions.text: Save an absolute LANE_CONFIG selection, or null for discovery, in the settlement receipt and bind every child environment to it.
decisions.why: The same relative string can select a missing or different file in a linked worktree. Retaining the intake selection also prevents a retry's working directory or environment from changing the accepted request.

decisions.text: Reproduce both findings before fixing production code and give every new test its own ORG_ACTOR.
decisions.why: Observed review failure and a spurious correction demonstrate that the behavioral regressions detect both defects. Actual Git, record, validation and review code exercise the fixes under explicit actor context.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: promoted to main after reviews r1-r4 (review-codex; each narrower: r1 two Majors, r2 one, r3 one, r4 none) and r5's diff checked directly (LANE_CONFIG resolved once and pinned; review gets a routes snapshot). One command settles a run: confirm the recorded report, check the diff, independent review on a review route, then promotable, a fix round (dispatch --reuse or fresh), or escalation with substance; never changes a newer run's outcome.
decisions.summary: settle promoted to main.

decisions.text: Hold a single installation mutex across recovery, planning, complete-plan validation and application, with durable write intent and runtime ownership tokens.
decisions.why: A later stale transaction must never interpret a successful predecessor's matching bytes or runtime as its own rollback work.

decisions.text: Keep startup file contents as buffers and encode owned receipts as base64, while accepting existing installed shell receipts.
decisions.why: Installation, upgrades, rollback and restoration must preserve operator bytes even when those bytes are not valid UTF-8.

decisions.text: Include the lane review template explicitly and include the newly landed settlement module in stable entry runtimes.
decisions.why: Installed supervisor commands must retain their code and data dependencies after Herdr relocates its build checkout.

decisions.text: Use a thin foreground module around the existing record, discovery, settle and promote implementations.
decisions.why: Discovery already establishes the supervisor role and the modules already own execution; the missing work is compact continuity, notice routing and durable mechanical receipts, not another scheduler or resident executive.

decisions.text: Route final report notices into settle and leave intermediate notices, substantive escalations and promotion authority to supervisor judgment.
decisions.why: Independent review belongs on the project review route; valid fix rounds are already dispatched by settle. A worker outcome or report-file existence cannot grant promotion or determine scope.

decisions.text: Complete promoted work through a current-run guard checked inside the record transaction.
decisions.why: A delayed promotion outcome must not close a newer run, unresolved or declined blocker, waiting outcome or concurrent work. Status remains derived from existing events.

decisions.text: Replace the handwritten kickoff with the generic protocol and retain only project purpose, source pointers and project scope.
decisions.why: Phases, routes, operator instructions, priorities and plans belong in durable record or configuration sources. The legacy launchers, contrib watcher and bch-cloak kit remain compatibility surfaces pending their existing migration gate.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: first live use of settle (on R-95, ENG-80): recorded the report, gated, reviewed on review-codex (NEEDS-WORK, two Majors), and dispatched the fix round R-97 itself with a watcher, in one command. The supervisor's hand steps for a report are now one call plus reading its JSON.
decisions.summary: settle module proven live.

decisions.text: Replace the socket syscall blacklist with explicit synchronous runtime syscall allowances and a default EPERM verdict.
decisions.why: The round-three instruction authorizes this boundary fix; io_uring, socket creation, BPF, ptrace and unknown syscalls receive no allowance, and incompatible ABIs fail closed.

decisions.text: Use a foreground native owner to clean every owned validation descendant across sessions and process groups, with kernel identity checks before signalling.
decisions.why: The round-three instruction requires positive ownership. Linux adopts orphans as a subreaper; macOS identifies the inherited private read policy and uses audit-token PID generations. Unknown processes are never cleanup targets.

decisions.text: Defer the macOS Claude guard until live execution is required and cover allocation, installation and evidence creation with cleanup.
decisions.why: Pending-only probes must work without authentication on Linux, and setup failures must not leave installed snapshots or copied project roots.

decisions.text: Keep both unexecuted Claude live cases classified as PENDING.
decisions.why: HUM-19 remains the operator prerequisite. No missing live session is counted as a code failure or successful acceptance.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: review r3 NEEDS-WORK (.lane/reviews/claude-discovery/8399269-r3.md), both findings in the Linux bubblewrap provider, which cannot be proven on this Mac (ENG-92 needs a Linux host). Decision: ship the Linux provider disabled by default (explicit experimental opt-in, documented) until ENG-92 proves it on Linux; round 4 fixes what applies to the macOS/Codex paths and records the Linux findings on ENG-92. Reversible.
decisions.summary: Linux sandbox provider off by default until proven on Linux.

decisions.text: Retain one first inspected byte-and-mode snapshot per destination and reject later differences across the complete inspected set before publishing the journal.
decisions.why: Ownership checks and replacement plans must refer to the same state, including destinations that require no write.

decisions.text: Share sanitized installation environments across both release-test invocation paths and verify an inherited parent installation through a complete child suite.
decisions.why: Supported machine overrides must remain usable in the product while offline release fixtures stay inside their own scratch destinations.

decisions.text: Compare worker tab creation, agent starts and worker prompts across completed settlement retries while retaining exact recorded-run and result assertions.
decisions.why: An independent detached watcher's concurrent reads and supervisor notices are not evidence of duplicate worker dispatch.

decisions.text: Enforce expected promotion heads in the promote module and shared lane execution path, and have supervisor pass the settled head and authorized run.
decisions.why: The queue must protect every caller that binds reviewed work; checking only in supervisor before enqueue cannot protect a lane that changes while pending.

decisions.text: Refuse rebasing of a bound head and fast-forward the validated commit directly.
decisions.why: Automatic rebasing would replace the authorized commit, and merging a moving branch name could integrate different work after the check.

decisions.text: Recheck current run, recorded done report, lane identity, closure, unresolved or declined blockers, changed outcome and overlapping work before integration under the record lock.
decisions.why: A guarded record close after promotion is too late to protect the promotion judgment; record changes during validation must prevent integration itself.

decisions.text: Return a resumable stopped handoff immediately before correction dispatch or incomplete-dispatch retry when canonical STOP exists.
decisions.why: Review can outlast a stop request; retaining its evidence and incomplete stage permits an explicit continuation without another review or worker launch.

decisions.text: Allow explicit promotion retry only after confirmed refusal and save prior attempts with their queue results.
decisions.why: Transient refusals need a recoverable new binding, while success, pending jobs and uncertain external effects must never be replayed blindly.

decisions.text: Verify correction idempotency using worker launches and correction prompts instead of all Herdr calls.
decisions.why: The acknowledged background watcher legitimately performs later reads and final-notice delivery; these calls do not prove duplicated correction dispatch.

decisions.text: Use one persistent suite group leader, keep fixtures in that group, and perform ordinary group teardown on every result.
decisions.why: One known live anchor covers fixture descendants after their parents exit, including children spawned before any helper can record their identities.

decisions.text: Remove guardian/reaper roles, SIGSTOP, ancestry discovery, registration journals and ancestor forwarding; make the final audit report surviving group members without signalling them individually.
decisions.why: Those mechanisms created ordering and recovery failures while trying to maintain a changing process tree. Inherited group membership supplies the required containment without that state.

decisions.text: Keep fresh start-time and full-command checks immediately before every helper PID or group signal, and report refused or unconfirmed cleanup.
decisions.why: The operator's earlier hard rule remains in force; other agents and operator sessions must not be exposed to historical PID or group signals.

decisions.text: Contain Node daemon launchers through a test-only preload and leave native kernel-sandboxed fixtures inside their existing boundary without that preload.
decisions.why: Product launchers need their IPC and lifecycle behavior tested without detached descendants escaping the suite; kernel attack fixtures remain synchronous, bounded, and do not launch detached children.

decisions.text: Await bounded concurrent fixture completion, then confirm watcher shutdown, before removing settlement fixture directories.
decisions.why: Cleanup was registered before the concurrent child hooks. Directory removal could run while a child was still writing; an unconfirmed child completion must leave the directory intact.

decisions.text: Compare the exact before-state first and restore the exact after-state before allowing the exception for original bytes with a caller's distinct mode.
decisions.why: Applied mode-only replacements must roll back while untouched files and separate operator chmods retain their current state.

decisions.text: Inject failures and process termination at the actual shell replacement boundary in isolated scratch installations.
decisions.why: Both synchronous rollback and subsequent recovery need executable evidence of permissions restoration, staged-file cleanup and retained surrounding installation state.

decisions.text: Require experimental-bubblewrap followed by an absolute executable path as the explicit validator selector, and remove all automatic bubblewrap discovery.
decisions.why: The supervisor's scope decision and R-99 instruction authorize this gate until the Linux provider's outstanding findings and proof are resolved on ENG-92. Ordinary paths and symlink aliases cannot activate the adapter implicitly.

decisions.text: Preserve existing native Codex installation defaults and make Linux auto validation refuse with the supported-provider and experimental-selection instructions.
decisions.why: Without an opt-in, validation must use the existing provider or refuse clearly; it must never execute an ordinary shell as a fallback.

decisions.text: Verify the reviewed behaviors on the actual macOS and native Codex paths while leaving Linux mount and syscall repairs to ENG-92.
decisions.why: This Mac can prove file copying and outside-write refusal for those providers, but cannot establish the Linux kernel boundary.

decisions.text: Keep unexecuted live Claude cases PENDING under existing HUM-19.
decisions.why: The operator prerequisite remains unanswered and this run's evidence is offline.

decisions.text: supervisor-herdr: code promoted to main (on retry after a settle record-safety test flake) after reviews r1 (FAIL), r2, r3 (review-codex) and r4's diff checked directly (bubblewrap only by explicit experimental-bubblewrap:/abs/path; never auto-discovered; plain bwrap refused). Validation runs without Codex on macOS; Git filters handled; privileged paths checked no-follow. ENG-81 stays blocked: live Claude proof waits on HUM-19 (operator), Linux proof on ENG-92.
decisions.summary: claude-discovery promoted to main.

decisions.text: Recover completed promotions before settlement and share the existing promotion-notice completion handler.
decisions.why: Completed queue work can lose its checkout; both notice orders must rely on bound receipts and retain the same integration and record guards.

decisions.text: Share the supervisor-entry contract assertion with the offline installed-adapter test.
decisions.why: The old watcher-path assertion rejected valid entry policies and was outside the inherited npm gate; testing the actual cold-start and notice contract through one assertion prevents that drift.

decisions.text: Require verified suite-group membership and the exact fixture command before adopting receipt PIDs, and retain accepted birth tuples across retries.
decisions.why: This closes reuse before registration without adding descendant hunting or a process journal to the live-group design.

decisions.text: Complete the isolated housekeeping schedule's teardown before the fixture directory hook on failure as well as success.
decisions.why: Cleanup must be installed before startup assertions and run while its fixture still exists.

decisions.text: Exercise both actual receipt readers with injected replacement identities, and temporarily bypass only the adoption guard in disposable negative-control copies.
decisions.why: Deterministic PID reuse verifies both rejection conditions and retained retry ownership without depending on the host PID allocator.
